Solution 7 (Coordinate Geometry)[edit]

We begin by scaling the diagram by and establishing a coordinate system. Recall the incenter formula . Here is our setup: \begin{align*} A&=(6,3\sqrt{21})\\ B&=(0,0)\\ C&=(16,0)\\ X&=(x,0)\\ AX&=\sqrt{(x-6)^2+189}\\ I_1&=\left(\frac{21x}{15+x+AX},\frac{3\sqrt{21}x}{15+x+AX}\right)\\ I_2&=\left(\frac{96+11x+16AX}{33-x+AX},\frac{3\sqrt{21}(16-x)}{33-x+AX}\right) \end{align*} We proceed by computing with the Shoelace Formula. Let . We have \begin{align*} [AI_{1}I_{2}]&=\frac{1}{2}\left\lvert 6\left(\frac{cx}{D_1}-\frac{c(16-x)}{D_2}\right)+\frac{21x}{D_1}\left(\frac{c(16-x)}{D_2}-c\right)+\frac{96+11x+16AX}{D_2}\left(c-\frac{cx}{D_1})\right) \right\rvert\\ &=\frac{c}{2D_1D_2}\left\lvert 6xD_2-6(16-x)D_1+21x(16-x-D_2)+(96+11x+16AX)(D_1-x) \right\rvert\\ \end{align*} To simplify, we see that \begin{aligned} 6xD_2&=198x-6x^2+6xAX\\ -6(16-x)D_1&=-1440-6x+6x^2-96AX+6xAX\\ 21x(16-x-D_2)&=-357x-21xAX\\ (96+11x+16AX)(D_1-x)&=1440+165x+336AX+11xAX+16AX^2\\ D_1D_2&=6(120+x+8AX) \end{aligned} Adding yields the terms in the absolute value: Hence, the result simplifies to Clearly the expression obtains its minimal when , this follows that Scaling the area yields .
